=== FILE: 3 DEADLIFT MISTAKES TO AVOID ⚠️ [afiPgBSiKzk].en.txt ===

Three common mistakes that people do deadlifting. Number one, people who deadlift too heavy tend to get down there, get ready to do the weight, and they can't really move it. Okay? You want to be able to move through the repetitions. You want to get that feel. Remember, it's not only going to focus on your back, going to be your hamstrings, your glutes, everything. Number two, the body position. You want to touch the bar to your shins almost to the point where the bar drags over the shins. Okay? You want to pull through the body, keeping your head up. Keep the body position and pull the weight almost like you're pulling their bar straight through your body. The third and final mistake is rounding the back. You want to go through the movement. You want to bend the knees a little bit. A lot of people tend to bend over and they round the back. Okay? Which you're going to end up with a back injury that way. You never want to round your back. You want to keep the chest high and like I said, pull through the body, okay? Do not round the back. Okay. My head stays up.

is the standard pull down with a machine the same thing as a pull-up I would say not I would say the ultimate back Builder you want to build Crazy wide lats you've got to stick to your pull-ups whether it's body weight or adding some weight to your body it depends how heavy you are more importantly there's nothing that will replace the standard pull-up you see all the wide backs all that V taper it comes from a wide pull down movement and that is best done on a pull-up bar not to say the pull Downs on a machine don't work but try to stick to the basics and do your pull-ups in your routine just make sure you focus on at least 10 repetitions I know it gets a little heavy sometimes especially as you just set up their set but remember the repetitions are gonna get the growth in the latch

=== FILE: FLAT VS INCLINE WHICH BUILDS A BIGGER CHEST [npMDE3Put20].en.txt ===

Everyone always asks what the best exercise for chest training is. Is it the incline press or is it the flat bench press? Now, the granddaddy exercise of all movements is the flat press. It's the first exercise you start to train with. I always was going for the bodybuilding, the repetitions. Anyone that goes and does the bench press, it signifies your strength, your manhood. I always incorporate some sort of this movement into my training routine to focus on the upper chest. You should do both. Whether you do one one workout, one the next, sometimes alternate. Everyone thinks their upper chest is going to grow from the incline. Yes, you're going to target a little more of the front delt, a little more of the upper chest when you do that incline, but I feel the flat bench can benefit just as much. Remember, keep your repetitions on eight plus and don't go extremely heavy. If you're smart and utilize it, you can build that full round chest and of course dominate if you want to get on stage.

=== FILE: Flat Bench VS Incline Bench [naGSEpK9MKM].en.txt ===

=== FILE: JAY CUTLER SPIDER CURLS FOR PEAK BICEPS [1oybQmXoq2U].en.txt ===

One of my favorite arm exercises which I use for my 2009 comeback to really focus and isolate the biceps are the spider curls just to curl up control little pause at the top. Remember the weight doesn't have to be super heavy for these. It's more of a contraction isolation movement. Nice and controlled. The Jbells make it so much easier. I am supernating the wrists a little If you notice, the palms are facing in and turn on the way up. Focus on the technique and don't worry about the weight so much. Now, remember, these can be done with cables. They can be done with a barbell, cambered bar. I prefer to use dumbbells and ideally I'm using the Jbell just because it's a little more controlled. The weight is more stabilized. With these, we're still going to focus on the rep range. It's a very isolation movement. So you take the shoulders out of it nice and controlled.

=== FILE: JAY CUTLER USES THE STANDING BENCH PRESS [FTwl9fE0R8E].en.txt ===

A lot of gyms don't have this. This is a standing bench press. Now, we have the different handles on this. We want to stimulate different parts of the chest. We have our fans of the incline, the flat, or the decline. We can kind of benefit all of these, or we can just go straight and push on the back handles. Ideally, with this, just a little variation. I don't get to see these in every gym. It's a little change up day. What I really like about this movement is I feel like with a bar or even with dumbbells, you're restricted how far you can come down. Now I'm very flexible, so I can actually go a little deeper with the repetitions and then the contract out. So that's what's nice. === FILE: JAY CUTLER’S ALL-TIME FAVORITE MASS CYCLE [aUn8FIR5fVM].en.txt ===

And for me that worked the best. Recovery is key. We always look at the gym and say, "Oh, I'm I'm putting on size training in the gym." But the truth is is getting out of the gym and eating. Get on that consistent schedule. But I always say prioritize your fitness lifestyle every day. If you click on Instagram or Snapchat, Tik Tok, YouTube, Facebook, I'm getting up every morning doing cardio. This morning I did my fasted cardio. just 20 minutes elliptical, get the heart rate up, get the metabolism flowing, and then I eat my meals, and then I come and do some weights at some point during the day. Twice a day, I'm hitting my metabolism by weight training or cardiovascular. And a lot of times I'm doing cardio after weight training, too. So, 20 minutes fasted, 20 minutes postworkout, after the weights. Why do I do that? It's efficient for me. This is what I do. This my routine. I love it.

=== FILE: Reverse Grip vs Overhand ｜ Barbell Row [kWJ1qMw12FM].en.txt ===

reverse grip barbell row over the common overhand grip what I like about doing the reverse grip Barbara row this allows me to get better contraction in my lats okay you can really pull a lot deeper with the reverse grip I've done it many many different ways and I know people kind of are concerned about their biceps because it definitely engages more bicep when you're doing that reverse grip so you really have to use your fingers as hooks for this movement I like to use straps honestly and use usually pull the bar focus on 10 or 12 repetitions I mean you can go extremely heavy with this exercise I believe this is a core movement for building the lower lats obviously the thickness it allows you definitely to get a lot more pull and engage a lot of the different back muscles that you might not get from some of the other movements especially with an overhand grip

Now, I prefer to do these seated only because I feel like I can get better body position and obviously no swinging. But more importantly, I do almost like a front raise and a side lateral at the same time. And I feel like sometimes people are looking to do more a little more strict and really kind of isolate in a sense where I feel you kind of have to go through the motion. And you have to have like almost uh in between where it's a side lateral and a front raise. And I remember I had some of the biggest delts when I was training at full capacity. But you'll see it's kind of like a like a from the side and then come out a little bit from the front. Really get engage that shoulder. Now there's three heads to the deltoid. So there's the front, the side, and the rear. And I think that ideally you can not isolate one single head of the shoulder, but you kind of want to get that main focus on the side.
